findings.text: the same-line refusal keys on the FIRST field only: changed_paths as a second key after any field other than commits still parses with the field silently emptied (probed at the landed head: 'tests: ran via pytest; changed_paths: a.py' returns tests='ran via pytest' and changed_paths=[]), which is the same empty-changed-paths shape the promotion guard exists to catch; the §12 done-when clause 'a manifest line carrying a second key after the first value is reported rather than silently misparsed' is therefore met for the measured commits→changed_paths pair, not for the general shape.

the promotion guard still converts a ManifestParseError into a return via the (OSError, KeyError, ValueError) catch, so the done-when's 'feeding it the one-line form and requiring a refusal rather than a skip' is upheld at the parser boundary only — the refused one-line form never makes the guard itself speak; documented as a §12 follow-on, so recorded here as a provenance caveat rather than a defect of this node.

justifications.durability: The guarded thing is made to happen rather than inferred from suite success: the refusal path is asserted directly (test_guard_refuses_commits_followed_by_changed_paths_on_one_line requires ManifestParseError), the quiet paths are asserted (exact prose, ordinary colon, URL port, separate lines all parse), and the pre-repair false refusal is captured as a reproduction traceback in the run logs; I independently probed the refusal and the prose fix at the landed head and both behave as described. Docked one because the promotion-layer half of the measure — feeding the one-line form to the guard and requiring it to refuse rather than skip — is upheld at the parser unit boundary, not by driving the guard, and that guard still swallows the parse error as a return (promotion.py:503, a documented follow-on), so 'cannot be disarmed' is verified at parse time rather than observed through the guard.
justifications.evidence: Every claimed figure reproduces on disk: reproduction.log shows the pre-repair false refusal raising ManifestParseError and naming artifacts on line 2, consistent with the base parser's whole-vocabulary search; baseline.log carries 41 passed and after-commit.log 46 passed at zero failures, exactly the five added cases; all five tests are present in the file and their prose matches the evidence and plan records; I re-ran the file green at a descendant head (62 passed — later additions, no regression from the reviewed change); ruff is the same two findings before and after at line offsets shifted by the insertion (none added); audit-doc reports 0 errors for both HTML documents; and all three claimed markers exist (_SAME_LINE_FIELD_PAIRS at reports.py:128, the exact prose regression test, and the manifest-prose-word-not-top-level-key anchor). Docked one: the after-suite was executed at the parser commit ac8621b rather than the full landed head 8b54439, so the HTML landing rests on audit-doc alone, and the base reference suite was read from its log rather than re-executed.
justifications.fit: The fix implements exactly the design tension §12 records — narrow the same-line refusal to the unambiguously structural machine pair, never treat authored prose as structure — with reproduction-first evidence (defect shown before repair), a five-case regression matrix, and a well-formed cumulative-evidence anchor and plan landing comment whose figures match the committed diff (57 insertions and 11 deletions across one source and one test file; 41-to-46 focused gate; zero failures either side). Commits use clean conventional subjects with bodies and no plan labels or attribution. Docked two: the first-key-only discriminator leaves the done-when's general clause unmet for the residual shape (any non-commits field followed by changed_paths still silently empties it — my probe), which the evidence section does not disclose, mitigating without disclosing a known fail-open; and the promotion guard's refusal-swallow means the 'speaks' half of the measure is asserted rather than shown.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The named defect — the second-key check firing on free prose — is fixed and the protection preserved: at the landed head the exact false refusal ('tests: ran the suite; artifacts: none were produced') parses whole as the tests value, the measured machine pair (commits: ...; changed_paths: ...) still raises ManifestParseError naming the line and both keys, and the separate-line form is unchanged; the promotion guard cannot be disarmed by the measured one-line form because that form is now refused at parse time rather than mis-parsed to an empty changed_paths. Docked one because the refusal keys on the first field only: changed_paths as a second key after any other field (probe: 'tests: ran via pytest; changed_paths: a.py' parses with changed_paths silently empty) is the same empty-changed-paths shape the section's guard exists to prevent, so the done-when's first clause is met for the measured pair, not in general.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exactly the four declared write paths appear across the two commits — reckon/crew/reports.py, tests/test_manifest_parse_format.py, docs/evidence/archive/crew-observability-truth-landed.html, docs/plans/crew-observability-truth.html — and nothing else; the run's own worktree HEAD is exactly the reviewed 8b54439 and clean (git status empty); the worker did not push or merge — the commits reached main only through the coordinator's merge, and 8b54439 is an ancestor of this node's HEAD; ruff and formatting were scoped to the changed file alone.
